title: Server Admin
description: Configure Damselette for your server and switch on protection against raids and mass destruction.

commands.name: config
commands.summary: Choose where moderation cases are logged and review your settings.
commands.description: Holds Damselette's general server settings. Set a mod-log channel so every case is posted in one place, and view all current settings at a glance, including those from the ticket system.

subcommands.name: modlog
subcommands.description: Every moderation case is posted as an embed in this channel, showing the case number, user, moderator, reason and any duration.

options.name: channel
options.description: The text channel that will receive the mod log.

subcommands.name: view
subcommands.description: Displays the mod-log channel, ticket panel channel, ticket category, support role, ticket log channel and the maximum open tickets per member.
notes: Only you can see the reply.

commands.name: antinuke
commands.summary: Protect the server from raids, nukes and rogue staff.
commands.description: Manages Damselette's anti-nuke protection and its raid guard. When someone who is not trusted breaks the limits, Damselette undoes the damage, can quarantine their power roles and asks your administrators to decide the punishment. When a flood of brand new accounts joins at once, it asks whether to lock the server down. Anyone with Administrator can view the status, but only the **server owner** can change settings, so a hijacked admin account can't switch protection off.
commands.access: Administrators can view `status`, `raid status` and the lists. Every other subcommand is for the **server owner** only.

subcommands.name: status
subcommands.summary: Show settings and check Damselette's permissions.
subcommands.description: Displays whether protection is on, the punishment, the alert channel, trusted users, staff roles, quarantine state and every limit. It also checks Damselette's own permissions and role position and lists anything that needs fixing.
notes: Run this after setup. A green check means everything is in order.
Only you can see the reply.

subcommands.name: enable
subcommands.description: Switches protection on. It is enabled by default on every server.

subcommands.name: disable
subcommands.description: Switches protection off. The server is no longer watched until you enable it again.

subcommands.name: punishment
subcommands.summary: Choose what happens when an admin approves a breach.
subcommands.description: Sets the action taken against an offender **after an administrator approves** the request. Damselette never applies it on its own.

subcommands.name: logchannel
subcommands.summary: Choose where anti-nuke alerts are posted.
subcommands.description: Approval requests and rollback reports are posted in this channel. Pick one your administrators watch closely. If none is set, Damselette falls back to your mod-log channel or system channel.

subcommands.name: limit
subcommands.summary: Adjust how much of an action is allowed.
subcommands.description: Changes how many times a non-trusted user may perform a protected action inside a time window before it counts as a breach. Setting the maximum to `0` makes the action never allowed.

options.name: action
options.description: The protected action to change, such as Channel deletes or Member bans.

options.name: max
options.description: How many are allowed inside the window, from 0 to 50. `0` means never allowed.

options.name: seconds
options.description: The window length in seconds, from 5 to 600. Keeps the current window if omitted.

examples.note: Allow three bans in any 30 second window.

notes: See the [Anti-nuke guide](#/docs/antinuke) for every protected action and its default.

subcommands.name: quarantine
subcommands.summary: Toggle instant removal of power roles on a breach.
subcommands.description: When on, the moment a breach is detected the offender temporarily loses only the roles that carry powerful permissions. They are not banned. If an admin dismisses the request, or it expires, the roles are returned.

options.name: enabled
options.description: `true` to quarantine offenders, `false` to only roll back and ask admins.

subcommands.name: relax
subcommands.summary: Give one person higher limits for a short time.
subcommands.description: Triples a person's limits for a limited period, handy when they are doing a big cleanup or responding to a raid. Use `off` to cancel early.

options.name: user
options.description: The person to relax limits for.

options.name: duration
options.description: How long, such as `30m` or `2h` (maximum 24 hours), or `off` to cancel.

examples.note: Three times the limits for two hours.

subcommands.name: staffrole
subcommands.summary: Manage roles that receive higher limits.
subcommands.description: Members of a staff role get double limits so everyday moderation never trips protection. They are still watched, and actions that are never allowed stay never allowed. Staff slack only applies after a member has been in the server for seven days.

examples.note: Administrators can also run the list view.

subcommands.name: raid
subcommands.summary: Manage join-flood detection and the lockdown it can raise.
subcommands.description: Anti-nuke watches what people destroy; the raid guard watches what arrives. When several brand new accounts join inside a few seconds, Damselette alerts your administrators without touching anybody. Approving that alert locks every text channel for `@everyone` while explicitly allowing your staff roles to speak, and everything is put back exactly as it was when the timer ends. Members of a staff role are never counted as raid traffic.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Turns join-flood detection on or off (for `mode`).

options.name: joins
options.description: How many fresh accounts inside the window count as a raid, from 1 to 100 (for `threshold`).

options.name: seconds
options.description: The window length, from 5 to 300 seconds. Keeps the current one if omitted.

options.name: age
options.description: Only count accounts younger than this many days, from 1 to 365. Established accounts are ordinary traffic and are never counted.

options.name: duration
options.description: For `lockdown`, how long an approved lockdown lasts. For `lock`, how long to lock now, or `off` to lift one.

examples.note: Shows the settings and whether a lockdown is running.
Busier server: only a flood of twenty new accounts alerts.

notes: Detection is on by default with 10 accounts younger than 7 days inside 10 seconds, and a 30 minute lockdown.
A lockdown denies Send Messages, Send Messages in Threads, Add Reactions and Embed Links to `@everyone` in text channels only. Voice channels, categories and threads are untouched.
Staff roles — the ones from `/antinuke staffrole add` plus any role that can manage, ban, kick, moderate or delete messages — are explicitly allowed through.
Nothing is done to any account: raid members stay in the server, they simply cannot post until the lockdown ends.
Needs **Manage Channels** and the Server Members Intent. See the [Anti-nuke guide](#/docs/antinuke).

subcommands.name: whitelist
subcommands.summary: Manage users and bots that anti-nuke always trusts.
subcommands.description: Trusted users and bots are ignored by protection. Whitelisting a bot also lets it be added to the server. The server owner is always trusted.

options.name: user
options.description: The user or bot to trust or stop trusting (for `add` and `remove`).

examples.note: Administrators can also run the list view.

notes: Only whitelist accounts you fully trust, because protection will not act on them.
For rollback and approved punishments to work, drag Damselette's role to the **very top** of your role list.
Read the [Anti-nuke guide](#/docs/antinuke) to understand how detection, approval and rollback work.
